A0157.title: Zero-Knowledge KYC and Privacy Protection
A0157.definition: Using zero-knowledge proofs to complete identity verification, proving compliance without exposing specific information.
A0157.description: Privacy-preserving KYC: zk-SNARK proofs for age/nationality; selective attribute disclosure; off-chain verification with on-chain proof; regulatory auditability; user-controlled data.
A0157.limitation: High technical complexity, unknown regulatory acceptance, and high computational cost. If vulnerabilities exist in the zk-SNARK proving circuit, attackers can forge compliance proofs to bypass KYC checks. Additionally, when off-chain data sources are falsified, the on-chain proof cannot detect the fraud, introducing risks of cryptographic compromise and source-level deception.
